event.details: Mudgala describes seven cosmic-egg worlds Bhūr, Bhuvar, Svar, Mahar, Jana, Tapo, Satya. Bhūr is the walking-accessible seven-island region illuminated by Sun/Moon; Bhuvar runs from Bhūr to Sun, Svar from Sun to Dhruva with corresponding Bhūr extent. Eight Vāyu divisions are Āvaha, Pravaha, Annavaha, Saṃvaha, Vivaha, Parāvaha, Parivaha, Vaha. Distance sequence in yojanas: Earth→Sun 100000, Sun→Moon 100000, Moon→stars 100000, stars→planet zone 200000, planet zone→ṛṣi zone 100000, ṛṣi zone→Dhruva 100000. Dhruva is axis of luminary wheel, holding wind-rays and moving stars. These are source cosmography, not modern astronomical measurements.

event.details: Sun maṇḍala extent 10000 and Moon 12000 yojanas; Rāhu 10000 below Sun, maṇḍala 13000. Darkness-formed Rāhu moves at parvan and rapidly covers Sun/Moon with shadow; called eclipse. Bhārgava’s maṇḍala is 1/16 Moon; Bṛhaspati 1/4 less than Bhārgava; Bhauma/Saura 1/4 less than Bṛhaspati; Saumya 1/4 less than those. Star/nakṣatra maṇḍalas successively 500/400/300/200, smallest star 1 ½ yojanas. Fractions preserved as stated, without calculated replacements.

event.details: Three distant slow planets named Saura, Aṅgirā, Bhauma lie above four fast planets Sun, Moon, Budha, Bhārgava. Ordering upward: Sun, Moon, stars, Kavi/Bhārgava, Budha, Bhauma, Bṛhaspati, Śanaiścara, seven ṛṣis, Dhruva. Sun travels two ayanas and governs planets. Bhauma is above Soma’s son, referring to Budha; only this explicit patronymic is normalized as parenthood, not an invented Bhārgava/Bṛhaspati family.

event.details: Sun chariot 9000 yojanas and shaft twice that; axle one lakh anchored at Dhruva, second axle’s wheel on Mānasā mountain. Wheel is zodiac/twelve-spoked; seven horses are metres led by Gāyatrī. Southward ayana is fast, northward slow. On Mānasā are east Indra’s Amarāvatī, south Dharmarāja’s Saṃyamanī, west Varuṇa’s Sukhā, north Kubera’s Vibhā. Sun dawn at Indra city, midday Yama, evening Varuṇa, midnight Kubera; potter-wheel-like movement gives direction-dependent perceived times.

event.details: Sun rays sustain people and fill three worlds, making day/night. Water, earth and sky and whole god/demon/human world arise, are supported and end in Sun. Enumerated deities, stars, fire, plants, Brahmins/water draw their radiance from him; he distributes all brilliance for play. Prabhākara is all-self/lord, Gaṇeśa portion, root of three worlds and karma-formed deity. This is source cosmological praise/support, not a universal biological genealogy.
